scope: Non-operational structural/computational hypothesis. No wet-lab protocol, pathogen engineering, or clinical treatment claim.
motivation: TOPA+Spider prior-art assault removed generic claims about hysteresis, time reversal, hidden states, asymmetry and capsid disassembly as already known. A narrower potentially testable cross-system rule remains.

candidate_law.name: PORTAL_OR_CONTACT_DUALITY
candidate_law.statement: For an icosahedral RNA virion, the useful reaction coordinate for directional genome egress should be anchored either by a dedicated symmetry-breaking portal/unique structural vertex, or, when no such dedicated portal is available, by asymmetric/non-equivalent cargo-shell interaction topology. Shell morphology alone should be insufficient in the latter class.
predictive_form: Given a pre-release structural/contact description, classify whether egress is expected to be portal-anchored or contact-topology-anchored before observing the release trajectory.
In contact-topology-anchored systems, early genome exposure/release should preferentially occur at loci or regions with weaker or reorganizing shell contacts, subject to context-dependent exceptions.
In dedicated-portal systems, the unique vertex should dominate the egress coordinate even when the global shell is nearly symmetric.
A system that fits neither class is a falsifying witness requiring expansion of the representation rather than post-hoc relabeling.

known_support_but_not_novelty: FHV: ordered RNA release and anti-correlation between release and RNA-capsid interactions; authors explicitly propose asymmetric RNA/contact organization as a determinant of release.
MS2/Qbeta and related phages: unique maturation/portal-like symmetry-breaking structures couple genome organization to release.
FCV: receptor-triggered unique VP2 portal-like assembly provides a dedicated release structure.
BMV: morphologically similar capsids with distinct RNA-capsid contacts exhibit different stability/release behavior.

already_known: viral symmetry breaking is biologically important
RNA-capsid interactions affect packaging and uncoating
FHV weak-contact loci are preferentially released
time irreversibility can expose hidden degrees of freedom in coarse-grained systems
prior_art_boundary.not_found_as_exact_general_law_in_curren: A single pre-specified classifier that treats dedicated-portal anchoring and cargo-contact anchoring as alternative reaction-coordinate classes and requires prediction before release data are exposed.

breakthrough_requirements: Freeze classification and release-origin/order prediction for a new system before its uncoating data are inspected.
Prediction must survive independent experimental or newly released data.
Repeat on a second independent virus system from a different family or architecture class.
Include a negative/control system where the classifier must decline or return UNKNOWN without false pattern forcing.
Run a dedicated novelty/prior-art review after confirmation.
Demonstrate that the rule changes model selection, experiment prioritization, or interpretation in a way experts could not obtain from shell-only analysis.
